# Overview

This guide describes the implementation of the Bayesian continual reassessment method (CRM) used in the accompanying manuscript. It covers:

- generation of true dose-response parameter values;
- specification and fitting of the Bayesian CRM;
- simulation of one illustrative trial;
- posterior updating after successive cohorts;
- prior-predictive evaluation;
- evaluation under five fixed dose-response scenarios;
- implementation of the rule-based comparator; and
- generation of operating-characteristic summaries, tables and figures.

The primary focus of this guide is the Bayesian CRM. The complete implementation
of the rule-based comparator is also provided in the accompanying repository.


# Software requirements

The analysis requires R, Stan and the following R packages.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

library(truncnorm)

```

# Dose-response model

The probability of infection at challenge dose $d$ is modelled as

$$
p(d)
=
1-
\left(
1+\frac{d}{b}
\right)^{-a},
$$

where $a>0$ and $b>0$.

The dose associated with target infection probability $p$ is

$$
ID_{p}
=
b
\left\{
(1-p)^{-1/a}-1
\right\}.
$$

The target probability is $p=0.70$; therefore, the target infectious dose is denoted by $ID_{70}$.


# Generate true parameter values

- True parameter values are required to simulate infection outcomes, and they are generated under two prior specifications:

1. Prior distributions on $a$ and $\log_{10}(ID_{70})$; and
2. Prior distributions on $a$ and $b$.

- Also, under these two prior specifications, true parameter values are generated for two cases:

1. Prior predictive evaluation
2. Scenario-based evaluation


## Parameter-generation functions

| Function | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `generate_prior_draws()` | Generates true values of $a$, $b$, and $ID_{70}$ under the selected parameter-generation specification. |
| `select_quantile_scenarios()` | Selects representative fixed scenarios at specified percentiles of the prior-generated $\log_{10}(ID_{70})$ distribution. |

: Functions used to generate true dose-response parameters. {#tbl-parameter-functions}

These functions are defined in:

```text
data_gen/param_helpers.R
```

## Parameter-generation settings

```{r}
#| label: parameter-generation-settings

target_prob <- 0.70

id70_settings <- list(
  a_lower = 0.3,
  a_upper = 0.8,
  log10_id70_mean = 4,
  log10_id70_sd = 0.8,
  log10_id70_lower = 3,
  log10_id70_upper = 7
)

ab_settings <- list(
  a_lower = 0.1,
  a_upper = 0.7,
  b_lower = 20,
  b_upper = 600
)
```

Under the primary specification,

\[
\log(a)
\sim
\operatorname{Uniform}
\{\log(0.3),\log(0.8)\},
\]

and

\[
\log_{10}(ID_{70})
\sim
N(4,0.8^2),
\]

truncated to \((3,7)\).

Under the alternative specification,

\[
\log(a)
\sim
\operatorname{Uniform}
\{\log(0.1),\log(0.7)\},
\]

and

\[
\log(b)
\sim
\operatorname{Uniform}
\{\log(20),\log(600)\}.
\]

## Generate parameter files

The following settings can be changed in `data_gen/generate_parameters.R`.

```{r}
#| label: generate-parameters
#| eval: false

prior_spec <- "id70_p"

generation_method <- "random"

target_prob <- 0.70

n_sim <- 1000

n_prior_draws <- 100000

scenario_percent <- c(
  0.05,
  0.25,
  0.50,
  0.75,
  0.95
)
```

For `generation_method = "random"`, one parameter set is generated for each
simulated trial.

For `generation_method = "scenarios"`, a large sample is generated and five
representative scenarios are selected at the requested percentiles of
\(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\).

The resulting files are saved in `data/`.

# Bayesian CRM implementation

## Core CRM functions

| Function | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `dr.model()` | Calculates infection probabilities at specified challenge doses under the beta-Poisson model. |
| `id.p()` | Calculates the dose associated with a specified infection probability. |
| `my.sim.fn()` | Simulates infection outcomes for one cohort at a specified dose. |
| `decision.criteria()` | Applies the posterior dose-allocation criteria and proposes the dose for the subsequent cohort. |
| `update_crm_model()` | Fits the Bayesian model using all accumulated cohort data and calculates posterior summaries at one interim analysis. |
| `run_bcrm()` | Runs repeated Bayesian CRM simulations for the prior-predictive or fixed-scenario evaluation. |

: Core functions used to implement the Bayesian CRM. {#tbl-bcrm-functions}

The functions are provided in:

```text
bayesian_crm/R/
```

## Candidate doses and trial settings

Five candidate challenge doses are considered:

\[
10^3,\ 10^4,\ 10^5,\ 10^6,\ 10^7
\quad \text{CFU}.
\]

The trial starts at \(10^4\) CFU and uses cohorts of five participants.

```{r}
#| label: crm-design-settings

target.doses <- 10^(3:7)

designs <- tibble::tibble(
  start.dose = 10^4,
  group.size = 5
)

N_cap <- 35

seed.no <- 250909
```

## Dose-allocation rules

After every completed cohort, the model is updated using all accumulated
infection outcomes.

At the most recently administered dose:

- escalate by one \(\log_{10}\) dose level if the 25th posterior percentile
  of the infection probability is below 0.60;
- de-escalate by one \(\log_{10}\) dose level if the 5th posterior percentile
  is above 0.80;
- otherwise remain at the current dose.

An accelerated escalation may be applied when the model-estimated \(ID_{70}\)
category is above the initially proposed dose. Any escalation is restricted to
no more than two \(\log_{10}\) dose levels.

## Stopping criteria

The capped design stops when either:

1. 20 participants have been challenged at the dose administered to the most
   recently completed cohort; or
2. the total sample size reaches 35.

The uncapped design applies only the first stopping criterion.

# Illustrative Bayesian CRM trial

One simulated trial is used to illustrate how the dose allocation and posterior
dose-response relationship evolve as infection outcomes accumulate.

## Illustrative-trial function

| Function | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `run_bcrm_example()` | Runs one selected simulated CRM trial, saves its cohort-level outcomes, and records posterior dose-response summaries after each interim analysis. |
| `create_fig_posterior_updating()` | Creates a multi-panel figure showing the prior and posterior dose-response relationship after successive cohorts. |

: Functions used for the illustrative CRM example. {#tbl-example-functions}

## Run one simulated trial

The example below uses Scenario 4 and simulation replicate 45.

```{r}
#| label: run-example-trial
#| eval: false

prior_spec <- "id70_p"
cap_method <- "capped"

example_scenario <- 4
example_sim <- 45

example_output_folder <- here::here(
  "bayesian_crm",
  "results",
  "examples",
  paste0(
    "scenario_",
    example_scenario,
    "_sim_",
    example_sim,
    "_",
    prior_spec,
    "_",
    cap_method
  )
)

example_results <- run_bcrm_example(
  scenario_no = example_scenario,
  sim_no = example_sim,
  prior_spec = prior_spec,
  target_prob = target_prob,
  id70_settings = id70_settings,
  ab_settings = ab_settings,
  cap_method = cap_method,
  N_cap = N_cap,
  seed.no = seed.no,
  start.dose = 10^4,
  group.size = 5,
  target.doses = target.doses,
  compiled_model = compiled_model,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 3000,
  warmup = 1000,
  save.output.to = example_output_folder
)
```

```{r}
  create_fig_posterior_updating(
    trial_dat = trial_dat,
    post_curves = post_curves,
    true_a =

    true_b =

posterior_updating_plot
```

The shaded bands represent pointwise posterior credible intervals for the
infection probability. The green dashed line represents the true dose-response
relationship, and the numbered points represent observed cohort outcomes.

# Prior-predictive evaluation

The prior-predictive evaluation assesses operating characteristics over a broad
range of possible true dose-response relationships.

One true parameter set is generated for each simulated trial. The design is
then evaluated across 1,000 simulated trials.

## Simulation function

| Function | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `run_bcrm()` | Runs the Bayesian CRM across independently generated true parameter sets. |
| `get_simulation_summary()` | Reads the output files and calculates summaries for one selected design and capping setting. |
| `get_all_simulation_summaries()` | Obtains rule-based and Bayesian CRM summaries under the requested capping settings. |
| `sum_bcrm()` | Calculates Bayesian CRM operating characteristics, including sample size, allocation, bias, RMSE, interval width and coverage. |
| `sum_rb()` | Calculates the corresponding summaries for the rule-based design. |

: Functions used in the prior-predictive evaluation. {#tbl-prior-evaluation-functions}

# Five fixed-scenario evaluation

Five representative scenarios are selected at the 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and
95th percentiles of the prior-generated distribution of
\(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\).

One thousand simulated trials are evaluated under each scenario.

## Fixed-scenario functions

| Function | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `select_quantile_scenarios()` | Selects the five representative dose-response scenarios. |
| `run_bcrm()` | Runs repeated Bayesian CRM simulations under each scenario. |
| `create_scenario_oc_tab()` | Constructs a table of sample size, interval width and participant-allocation summaries by scenario. |
| `create_scenario_performance_tab()` | Constructs a table of estimation performance, coverage and boundary-dose selection by scenario. |
| `create_fig_trial_size_5scn()` | Plots the distribution of total study size across the five scenarios. |
| `create_fig_target_5scn()` | Plots the distribution of participants allocated to the final administered dose across scenarios. |

: Functions used in the five fixed-scenario evaluation. {#tbl-scenario-functions}

# Rule-based comparator

The main focus of this guide is the Bayesian CRM. The conventional 5+5+10
rule-based design is included as a comparator.

## Rule-based functions

| Function | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `rulebased_path()` | Simulates one complete trial under the 5+5+10 rule-based design. |
| `run_rule_based()` | Runs repeated rule-based simulations under random parameter sets or fixed scenarios. |
| `sum_rb()` | Calculates sample-size, participant-allocation and dose-selection summaries for the rule-based design. |

: Functions used to implement and summarise the rule-based comparator. {#tbl-rule-functions}

The implementation is available in:

```text
rule_based/R/
```

The rule-based design can be run using:

```{r}
#| label: run-rule-based
#| eval: false

rule_based_results <- run_rule_based(
  cap_method = "capped",
  generation_method = "scenarios",
  prior_spec = "id70_p",
  n_sim_scenario = 1000,
  simulation_seed = 250909,
  n_cap = 35
)
```

The same true parameter files are used for the rule-based and Bayesian CRM
designs. A separate posterior-updating example is not required because the
rule-based design does not use a Bayesian posterior distribution.

# Operating characteristics

The simulation study evaluates:

- average and median total sample size;
- number of participants treated at the final administered dose;
- number of participants treated above the final administered dose;
- final dose-selection probabilities;
- mean bias of the posterior median of \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\);
- mean absolute error of \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\);
- RMSE of \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\);
- posterior credible-interval width; and
- coverage of the true \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\).

The final administered dose is defined as the dose administered to the final
cohort. The number treated at this dose includes all participants challenged at
that dose throughout the trial.

# Reproducibility

Random-number seeds are specified for:

- parameter generation;
- fixed-scenario selection;
- simulated trial outcomes; and
- prior-predictive graphical summaries.

The code uses project-relative paths constructed with `here::here()` and does
not rely on a user-specific working directory.

Computationally intensive chunks use:

```yaml
eval: false
```

This displays the implementation code without rerunning the full simulation
study when the guide is rendered.

# Reproducing all results

To reproduce the complete analysis:

1. Generate the random and fixed-scenario parameter files using
   `data_gen/generate_parameters.R`.
2. Run the Bayesian CRM simulations for the requested prior, generation method
   and capping setting.
3. Run the corresponding rule-based simulations.
4. Calculate operating-characteristic summaries using the functions in
   `fig_tables/R/`.
5. Generate the manuscript and supplementary tables and figures using the
   reporting helper functions.

The full simulation study requires repeated Stan fitting and may take
considerable computation time.
